title: Fix MCP App Build Rs Wasm Alias
description: `npm run mcp:inspector` fails in pre step `build:mcp-app` because Vite's worker-import-meta-url plugin tries to bundle `compose/js/worker.ts` (referenced via `new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` in `compose/js/index.ts`) and cannot resolve the virtual package `@semio-tech/compose-rs-wasm`. The other vite configs (sketchpad, react, js) already alias `@semio-tech/compose-rs-wasm` to `compose/rs/pkg`. Add the alias to `compose/engine/vite.mcp-app.config.ts` so the MCP app build succeeds. Verify `npm run mcp:inspector` starts.
summary:
Fixed `npm run mcp:inspector` build failure. The pre-step `build:mcp-app` (Vite build of the single-file MCP App) failed because Vite's worker-import-meta-url plugin tried to bundle `compose/js/worker.ts` (referenced via `new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url))` in `compose/js/index.ts`) and couldn't resolve the virtual package `@semio-tech/compose-rs-wasm`, plus the worker sub-bundle was forced into IIFE format by vite-plugin-singlefile's code-splitting defaults.

Changes to `compose/engine/vite.mcp-app.config.ts`:
- Added `resolve.alias` mapping `@semio-tech/compose-rs-wasm` → `../rs/pkg` (consistent with the sketchpad/js/react vite configs).
- Added `worker: { format: "es", rollupOptions: { output: { inlineDynamicImports: true } } }` to let the worker sub-bundle use ES modules and inline its dynamic imports (required because singlefile disables code-splitting).

Build result: `mcp-app.html` (4.1 MB) is a clean single-file HTML with no external worker reference (the worker chunk is tree-shaken out of the HTML because the MCP viewers never call `createKitStoreClient`). `dist/worker-*.js` is still emitted as a sibling chunk but unreferenced — harmless.

Runtime note: Port 6274 (the @mcpjam/inspector default) is currently held on the Windows host by Cursor's remote-containers port forwarder (PID 98704, parent Cursor.exe) which forwards the devcontainer's port 6274 to the host. That means an MCP inspector is already running inside the devcontainer and accessible at http://localhost:6274 — so running `mcp:inspector` a second time on the host will fail with "Port 6274 is already in use". The @mcpjam/inspector CLI has a `--port` flag but its 1.x code ignores it (hardcodes 6274), so changing the port isn't viable from the npm script. Per CLAUDE.md the IDE port forwarder must not be killed.
